note: Documents that satisfy site-inventory.v1 completely and are still ambiguous. Each one is the smallest inventory carrying the semantic-key rule it breaks, and each is asserted schema-valid before it is asserted semantically invalid — that assertion is the proof that JSON Schema does not enforce these relationships and that uniqueItems would not help. Violations are (pointer, rule) pairs only; no free text is recorded. The digests are synthetic fixture data, and a document in this directory cannot have a real one: the whole point is that it has no canonical ordering to digest.

duplicate-source-id.proves: One attempted discovery source is reported once. Two entries for SITEMAP with different outcomes satisfy the schema — the array carries no uniqueItems, and uniqueItems would not catch this anyway because the entries differ as whole objects — while leaving a candidate's provenance naming SITEMAP resolvable to two contradictory outcomes and the canonical ordering of sources with a tie it can only break by input order.

duplicate-candidate-url-key.proves: One canonical identity appears once in the candidate population, because observations that share an identity aggregate onto one candidate. Two candidates carrying the same url_key with different observed_forms are distinct whole objects, so uniqueItems passes, and the population is left with two entries a consumer must choose between and an output digest that depends on which order the producer emitted them in.
